text_fidelity_a:
Steiner Sports MLB New York Yankees Authentic Yankee Stadium "Freeze Dried Grass" Sod w/ Glass Display Case I should have listened to the other 2 reviewers. I am beyond disappointed in the condition of this item. First of all, the fact that all the pieces were separate would not have been an issue IF the items were packed properly. The piece of sod was thrown haphazardly into a very thin plastic bag that was completely wide open and not secured closed at all. There is almost as much dirt and grass in the bottom of the bag as there is on the piece of sod. I'm surprised that there isn't dirt and grass all over the box it was thrown into as well. Worst of all, the sod is absolutely NOTHING like the picture. it is a 3 inch round piece of mostly dirt, that is not a rich dark brown as pictured, but a dried-out, tan-colored crumbling mess. And, the grass is long, sparse and a mix of pale green, yellow and brown. Not sure what the freeze-drying process is supposed to do, but the grass and dirt are so dry that you can't even breathe near it without pieces of grass and dirt falling off. What a mess! AND it smells pretty nasty too.

The letter of authenticity is trash (or at least it is to Steiner). It was thrown into the box along with the packing materials, without an envelope or any other protection. From being jostled around inside the shipping box, it is now crumpled and torn in at least three places along the side. Granted, it is a thicker-weight paper, but an envelope would have been nice (especially for the price). The letter says that the sod was removed on March 14, 2009 and that it is "unconditionally guaranteed" - whatever that means. It's difficult to tell if the signature of "Brandon Steiner" is signed in ink or a copy. I don't want to damage the signature trying to figure it out.

The case is actually a baseball case and comes in a "single baseball glass case" box. When I first opened the shipping box, I thought I'd been sent the wrong item. The case IS made of glass, not acrylic, and supposedly has a cherry wood base. It also is not nearly as nice as the picture depicts. The wood is dry and dull and the joints are roughly glued together and uneven. Unlike one of the other reviewers (and the description), I did not receive a separate sticker to apply to the base. It actually has a metal plaque already attached. The problem is, the only words that are legible are "Yankee Stadium Artifact." There are three full lines of smaller writing below that but it is completely unreadable. I can't tell if the words got scratched off or if it was improperly printed on the plate to begin with. I cannot read what it says at all.

I'm not familiar with these types of cases, but there is nothing that holds the grass in place. The bottom is a slick mirror, and the slightest movement causes the sod to slide around inside the case, leaving dirt and debris all over the bottom. Unless its kept perfectly still, it will probably fall apart completely into a big mess in no time. My biggest regret is that I did not purchase this from Amazon. I paid only $59 from another source who is not nearly as easy to deal with. Although, I don't think it would have made a difference in the quality of the product or awful packaging, because this item ships directly from Steiner sports anyway.

I've posted over 80 product reviews on Amazon. This is the first time I've ever felt the need to post pictures or video. This item is so pathetic - you really have to see it to believe it, so I am going to post something tomorrow. I just wanted to post my review ASAP so that anyone considering buying this as a last-minute Christmas gift is forewarned. I initially felt too embarrassed to give this as a gift, but now I think the recipient might appreciate the "tragic humor" of this item. It would make a good conversation piece for sure! I will let him decide if he wants to return it for something else, or keep it as something to show to his friends and laugh about.
text_fidelity_b: Steiner Sports MLB New York Yankees Authentic Yankee Stadium "Freeze Dried Grass" Sod w/ Glass Display Case

Sunny Health & Fitness Twisting Stair Stepper Machine with Handlebar and Digital Display This just arrived so it's too soon to say, but I REALLY miss my Aspen stepper that lasted forever and would probably still be going strong if I hadn't lent it to my kids who left it out in the rain and ruined it.

PROS: It was relatively easy to assemble; it's made of steel rather than plastic; it has a built in timer (also a scan, calorie counter and stroke counter), but the accuracy of these things is dubious at best, and I'm not one to use them anyway; it doesn't take up much space and is easy to move.

CONS: The tension adjustment knob is a joke. From the easiest to the most difficult setting is so subtle, I barely noticed it. Even at the most difficult setting, going as fast as I could, I didn't perspire at all; for people who are used to steppers, the twisting motion is a bit awkward, and since it came with no exercise instructions, perhaps there's something I'm missing to the advantages of twisting; at full extension, the handle bars don't go up very high, and they don't move.

If you're someone just embarking on an exercise routine, don't want to spend a lot of money and don't have a lot of space, this will probably work just fine. However, for the athletically inclined who already work out regularly, this will probably be a bit of a disappointment.

Update: Have now had this for a while and need to mention that 1) the tension adjustment knob does work but ONLY WORKS IF YOU LET THE STEPPER SIT FOR AT LEAST A COUPLE OF HOURS. If you try adjusting it without letting is sit undisturbed, you will NOT feel any difference; and 2) the 250# weight limit is a joke. My husband, who weighs 195, can't use it at all. If he does, the cable screws (as others have commented) break off. He's handy, so he's been able to fix it each time, but after 3 or 4 times, he just will no longer use it. For me, it's not much of a work out, but I do use it.

Update a little over a year later: The cable broke, and the manufacturer has been unresponsive. So into the trash it sadly goes. Due to a major design flaw in construction, the cable is forced to stretch, wear down and eventually break with use over time. A hydraulic resistance system would be a major design improvement. So if you don't mind a machine that will only last about a year, this stepper is fine. But if you want something that will last longer, I'd give it a miss.
text_fidelity_b: Sunny Health & Fitness Twisting Stair Stepper Machine with Handlebar and Digital Display

text_fidelity_a:
MIER Lanshan Ultralight Tent 3-Season Backpacking Tent for 1-Person or 2-Person Camping, Trekking, Kayaking, Climbing, Hiking UPADATED AGAIN: I have purchased both the 1 and 2 person tent. Seems like very well quality and lightweight. However, the ONE thing that is bad about BOTH tents is the way the end tie outs are sewn and sealed. The tents BOTH leak at the tie out points. This is due to the way they are sealed. It seams as if the seam seal was applied FIRST and then the tie outs sewn into the fabric. This allows water to come through the stitching and leak into the tent. POOR DESIGN. I have remedied this by using seam sealant on ALL stitch points for the tie outs. So, word of caution for everyone owning and buying these tents. MAKE SURE YOU SEAM SEAL EVERY TIE OUT POINT. Once you do that, this tent should be waterproof.

UPDATE: I set this tent up in my yard to test it for waterproof and durability. We had a rain event that came through. No heavy storms. Just light to medium rain that only lasted 10 or 15 minutes. The tent leaked at both ends where the tie outs are sewn into the fabric. These points are seam sealed, so I do not know why or how it leaked at both points. The water on the floor of the tent was about the size of a quarter.
I have since sprayed all of the fly seams and the tie out points with silicone treatment. When we get another rain storm coming through, I will set it up again for another test to see if the spray will keep the tie out points from leaking.
Also, both sides and the rear of the fly, down at the edge, collect water and allow it to pool up. This is a design flaw. I had the tent as tight as I could get it, without damaging the material. The water pooled up around the bottom edge looked like a small moat, and could lead to large amounts of water to run under the tent. This could soak through the floor and get your sleeping gear wet.
I fixed this issue with some micro tarp clamps and 550 cord. I attached one at each end, and two in the rear, one on each side between the rear stake out point and each corner. So 4 total. When I set the tent up again for another rain test, I will update with pictures.
So far, this tent was NOT the tent that all the hype was about. The ONLY positive thing so far, is that it is a true double wall tent, and that will keep condensation out of the sleeping area.

I have not used this tent yet, only set it up. However, with just having set it up, I can see that I will probably like this tent. But, one thing I would like to have seen with it, is more fabric at the vestibule. When set up by the directions, the edge of the vestibule is quite high off of the ground. This would allow for good ventilation during a summer night, but in a rain storm, I would be afraid of rain being blown in.
I have it set up in the yard, and we have a chance of rain today/tonight, so once I let it get rained on and take it out on a trip, I will update my review.
text_fidelity_b: MIER Lanshan Ultralight Tent 3-Season Backpacking Tent for 1-Person or 2-Person Camping, Trekking, Kayaking, Climbing, Hiking

text_fidelity_a:
Retrospec Solstice Trekking & Ski Poles for Men & Women - Aluminum w/Cork or Foam Grip - Adjustable & Collapsible Lightweight Hiking, Walking & Skiing Sticks Good light, sturdy poles. They aren't cheap feeling. I am really quite impressed with the design, how they feel, and the overall options included. They come clipped together (keep the clips, or discard) tucked away in a nylon drawstring storage bag. The kit contains wide and narrow snow baskets and rubber boots/tip. Just screw on. Can choose to use none of those and just use the carbide tip. Can elongate both portions via a clip to your height needs. I am 5'10" and these are plenty long for me. They shorten down to manageable height for easy storage and carry. The carry bag has a shoulder strap.

I have used these for snow shoeing, XC/alpine skiing (not nordic/down hill- these are not meant for that), walking through snow in regular boots, walking in mixed dirt/snow/ice. They are really quite sturdy. They are way better than a pair of basic walking pole/sticks I had that broke on a trail within a couple of uses. I find the ones that are capable for snow use to be better. These are better priced than many too. I would/will recommend these!

My primary use though: I happen to have a long semi steep hill directly outside my back door. We have dogs, so we are always going down that hill to get to more leveled out ground. The soil is sandy and doesn't hold grass well. So we are missing a lot of grass and even where there is grass, it tends to get kicked up easily. So even on dry days it can be a slipping hazard. Now add in rain, mud, ice, snow.. and well you can understand what I am about to say next: trekking poles (and good boots) help. Use of poles add a little additional stability. I like to use mine with the large cups, for this purpose. Our winter thus far in NY has been pretty much spring like. Not enough snow to keep mud/ice at bay, not enough cold to keep things firmed up out there. I want my freezing days, and we have barely had any. No Almost no reprieve from mud and slop. So much potential slippage. So much dirty paw action! Ah well.

Bright spot is getting out to play with my dogs and using these to walk around the yard. I just use them for the hill, but once down to the level area, I mind as well keep on using them.. so in this sense I am getting an additional work out of the sort because I am using my arms to move these. I will continue to use these come spring/summer on my walks for that very reason (which is why I had walking sticks before.. for additional burn)

The product description did a great job describing these and the included pictures are spot on. I included a pics of my dogs on the hill. We aren't even to the bottom yet. You can see a little bit of the back of the house at top of hill. You see that the hill starts immediately. Many people have asked if we go sledding on this hill. At bottom of hill the land levels out for maybe 20 feet and butts up to a creek. The back yard is an adventurous place!-- and these multi use trekking poles are helping me navigate it in a more safe and steady manner. Yay!
text_fidelity_b: Retrospec Solstice Trekking & Ski Poles for Men & Women - Aluminum w/Cork or Foam Grip - Adjustable & Collapsible Lightweight Hiking, Walking & Skiing Sticks

text_fidelity_a:
Soddeph 1.3 Gallon Collapsible Water Container Bag, BPA Free Food Grade Clear Plastic Storage Jug for Sport Camping Riding Mountaineer,Freezable,Food Grade (1.3 Gal, 2-pack) As we live in a hurricane prone area we decided to add these to our preparedness collection. Along with our gallons of water we thought it would be a good idea to grab these. Unlike the gallon we’ll full these bags up last minute and use for cooking and cleaning water. They are very large and store a good amount of water, and with the their base that speaks out and sits well, it’ll be good to have around. But they don’t seem like they’ll be able to sit and hold water as we do for the entire 6 month season with our normal gallon jugs. No problem, again, we’ll fill them as a storm is approaching and use for short term storage.

The materials (plastic) seem like they’ll hold up. We have found with the gallon jugs there are quality differences: some are thin and will start to leak after a few months. We also do not keep them from season to season. As a season hits it’s end we’ll use that water for water and cooking and then restock for the next season. With these jugs we’ll fill as the storm approaches, then empty after it’s through and water is no longer needed.

I THINK I’ll be able to fill in the sink, but have not tried. It is large and we’d prefer doing a good cleaning on the sink before laying it inside. I did not take that time and instead filled it from the tub. That worked okay. I lost a good amount of water as the flow from that spigot is not great. But it filled in a few minutes and will sit fine.

Overall it’ll be a good back up and we’re happy to have them for our set up. Should we ever go camping (not something we do) or need water in a pinch, we’ll find other uses. But just the prep element is well worth having these around.
text_fidelity_b: Soddeph 1.3 Gallon Collapsible Water Container Bag, BPA Free Food Grade Clear Plastic Storage Jug for Sport Camping Riding Mountaineer,Freezable,Food Grade (1.3 Gal, 2-pack)

text_fidelity_a:
Kodiak Canvas Flex-Bow Canvas Tent Deluxe LOVE LOVE LOVE this tent!!!
We have previously owned the classic cheaper coleman tents and when ours wore out, we bought a new coleman... upon opening it, it had tears in the seams...I boxed it up and sent it back. We were so upset by the lack of craftsmanship we decided to research better quality canvas tents. We are a young family and liked the idea of a tent that we could use for years to come. We decided on the 10x14, it's very spacious and we are able to set up a queen, and twin air mattress with plenty of room to store our bags/totes and a large dog/bed. I am a petite lady and I was able to put this tent up by myself (only took 25 min from box to erect, while stopping to look at the directions) it is a very heavy tent, but I was able to put it up with a bit of effort.
Once up I was able to really get a look at this tent... WOW! This tent is large and heavy duty! The floor is a thick rubber-like material that you can tell isn't gonna leak (and it didn't, even when there were puddles of rain water between the tarp below and tent) I sprayed the tent down (as per directions) prior to our first camping trip. And off we went...
This tent has turned heads every time we camp, it is a heavy duty, quality tent that we know will last for years to come... It is so simple to put up, and we are so pleased with our investment.
We have not yet had it stand the test of a storm, but I have no doubt it will hold up well.
As far as staying warm, the larger tent makes it difficult to stay warm, so bundle up and use warm blankets ;)

Oh, did I mention the tent storage bag?!?! It's awesome, and your tent will always fit, no need for super tight refilling to make it fit in the bag, this bag adjusts and will always fit your rolled up tent (we fold in half, then half again, roll and adjust the bag to fit )

To summarize:
Pros:
Large roomy tent that you can stand and walk around in, the walls are straight so you don't lose storage room
Durable canvas that is waterproof
Quality thick floor that will not leak
Heavy duty metal rods/poles and steaks
Large doors and windows makes the tent feel even more open and allows a cross breeze
The ingenious tent bag that will always be able to fit the tent once rolled up

Cons:
The long poles (when storing) and the weight of the tent
No electrical slot for extension cords (have to put them through the door)

Overall If you are in the market for a quality tent that will last for years to come...buy this tent!
text_fidelity_b: Kodiak Canvas Flex-Bow Canvas Tent Deluxe

Elastic Foot Loops Resistance Bands Workout Bar, Yoga Bar kit, & Exercise Bar. Exercise is important, as I am sure most would agree. But often, it isn’t practical to pay a visit to a nearby gym- you need something that is easily accessible and that you can take with you, wherever you go, for a quick workout. A good option for your workout needs is Portable Pilates Bar Kit with Premium & Upgraded 30LB Thick Resistance Bands.

Pulled from the package, this workout equipment is ready to use. All you need to do is attach the ends of the workout bar. At this point, you can use the foot loops to hold it down, then start exercising. There are several different ways you can use this simple piece of equipment. It can be used to tone different muscle groups depending on how it is used.

You do get a fairly good amount of resistance from this workout bar, but there is no way to control the level of resistance. You have to take it the way it is, since there is no way to adjust it, that I can see. It seems to work fine for basic needs. Once you have used it for a while, I would guess that will no longer be sufficient- it will get too easy and you will likely need something with greater resistance. In other words, this cannot take the place of the sophisticated workout equipment in a well- stocked gym. But the best part about it is that, since it is so small and compact, you can use it whenever you need it.

The best way to utilize the Portable Pilates Bar is to find different ways to do the exercises. I recommend going online and looking for different exercises so that you can workout different muscle groups. It’s a nice, simple piece of exercise equipment and it is useful for those who are on the go and need something to encourage exercise anytime, anyplace.

text_fidelity_a:
Earth Therapeutics Mind/Body Therapy Anti-Stress Eye Pillow, Lavender + Chamomile, 1 pillow Good anti stress eye pillow. What I like about the Earth Therapeutics Mind/Body Therapy pillow
1) I like the fragrance of the lavender and chamomile pillow.
2) The fragrance is not overwhelming it is subtle.
3) It is not overstuffed so it drapes nicely over your eye and sinus area when you are lying flat.
4) The silk has a cooling effect
5) I have chronic sinusitis and this pillow feels like it helps to relieve some of that tight pressure pain. It also seems to calm the area around my eyes.
I have used several different sinus pillow type remedies over the years for that "ahhh relief!" moment when you can feel the swelling and ache diminishing.Not many were very effective but this one and the Lavender eye pillow by AyaZen are both effective. However, I would choose the one from AyaZen over this one because:
1) It can be heated and froze as long as you put it in a plastic sealed bag so it doesn't absorb freezer odor.
2) It has more filling and a more balanced filling making it a little weightier than the Earth Therapeutics eye pillow
3) The velvet like cover of the AyaZen is soft and luxurious yet it also has a griping effect so it doesn't readily slip off your face.
4) It has a stronger lavender scent that is soothing but not overwhelming.
5) For me, this pillow relieves the pain and pressure associated with my sinusitis better.

As a comparison, they are both good eye pillows but AyaZen wins for me.

The reason Earth Therapeutics is not a perfect five stars and doesn't win for me:
1) It doesn't have the balanced filling the AyaZen does
2) The silk used to encase the Earth Therapeutics pillow slips very easily unless you are lying down flat.If your head happens to turn a little while sleeping at an angle or with your head raised at any height, it slips off. Even though you can conform it to your eyes and nose it won't stay because of the silkiness of the material and the almost whisper light weight of the pillow. If your head is raised at any angle or your head happens to fall sideways while napping, you must continually reposition the pillow.
3) you cannot heat it in the microwave or put it in the freezer. I know this pillow is suppose to be Therapeutic based solely on the oils it harbors and the silk that encases it but it just needs a little more to really reach that Therapeutic level.

I bought this based on it conforming to the face and being Therapeutic. However, I often sleep with my head raised up or in my recliner because of breathing issues due to my sinuses.The silk of this pillow would always cause it to slip down or sideways causing me to wake up and recenter it on my eyes. Overall, I would recommend this pillow for someone who doesn't have to sleep with the head or upper body raised at any height and doesn't have to turn their head much while napping. The silk does have a cooling effect and the lavender and chamomile does help to relieve some of the pressure and pain.
text_fidelity_b: Earth Therapeutics Mind/Body Therapy Anti-Stress Eye Pillow, Lavender + Chamomile, 1 pillow

text_fidelity_a:
Bugleman Rifle Sling Staging Strap Magnetic Sling Staging Solution It’s a good concept, but the execution is poor for larger straps. If you store more than one fold of the sling the magnets aren’t powerful enough to hold on. When using a blue force sling it is basically useless. Regardless of where you try it, foregrip or the stock, it cannot hold the sling in place. A heavy duty rubber band is more effective than this at holding large straps.

I also believe the company is using a common practice of identifying an American made product, while not outwardly saying Made in America. I understand that an American flag doesn’t always mean made here, but this style is commonly used for such purposes. Seeing as the company's profile is based out of China I would safely say this product is made there.

Overall, I wouldn’t recommend this product for most. If your strap is very narrow and you would have at most one fold over it might work but be aware that if it rubs against something the magnets will let go. I would like to see the company use stronger magnets or possibly a small strip of Velcro to assist the magnets. In the meantime I will sew some Velcro to my existing one.
text_fidelity_b: Bugleman Rifle Sling Staging Strap Magnetic Sling Staging Solution

SukhaMat Yoga Knee Pad Cushion – America's Best Exercise Knee Pad - Eliminate Pain During Yoga or Exercise - Extra Padding & Support for Knees, Wrists, Elbows - The Perfect Yoga Mat Accessory NOTE: I received a free sample of this knee pad to review.

I practice yoga regularly and am currently about midway through a yoga teacher training program. I own several mats, with the one I use the most often being [[ASIN:B009LHXD3O Manduka EKO Lite]]. This mat is on the thin side--which I generally like--and yet there are times when I find a bit of extra padding to be supportive.

The length of the SukhaMat worked so that it fit across my entire yoga mat. The width seemed a bit narrow, as I found myself adjusting the placement of the pad during use. As promised, the mat definitely did provide cushioning, yet I found the density of the mat to be a bit too much on the "squishy" side rather than providing firm support. And although the mat is supposedly made of foam, I found that it gave off a bit of an unpleasant, rubbery scent.

In the end, I didn't find this mat to be more convenient than standard yoga props such as blankets or blocks. Even rolling it up with my yoga mat for storage/transport was a problem--when I did this, it made my yoga mat too bulky, and it caused the SukhaMat to curl up on the edges rather than to lie flat. I can't say that this mat worked well for me, but it may be better for others who are in need of a more cushy product.
text_fidelity_b: SukhaMat Yoga Knee Pad Cushion – America's Best Exercise Knee Pad - Eliminate Pain During Yoga or Exercise - Extra Padding & Support for Knees, Wrists, Elbows - The Perfect Yoga Mat Accessory

Compaclite High Back Oversize Steel Portable Chair for Outdoor Camping / Picnic / Hiking / Bicycling / Fishing / BBQ / Beach / Patio with Carry Bag, Royal Blue I’m torn with how to rate this chair. I have the 360 swivel version ($60) as well as this one, which is about half the price. This compaclite chair has a higher back which makes it more comfortable than the swivel version, and the pillow actually is a nice plus. It’s compact and more comfortable than typical folding chairs. When compared to the swivel version, this one wins no contest. However, it still isn’t enough for it to be bumped up to 5 stars, and I’ll tell you why.

As many others have mentioned, these chairs aren’t the sturdiest and wobble a bit. The drink holder is placed in an awkward place on the chair (right between your legs) and the chair does take a few minutes to set up, whereas a simple folding chair is done in a few seconds. I imagine this will get better with time, but it does take some elbow grease to get the corners of the chair into the poles. Although the pillow is quite comfortable and really nice, it makes folding the chair a bit more of a pain that the swivel version (because no pillow). One of compaclite’s best features is the fact that…yes…it’s compact, so the pillow adds a stressor that makes it difficult to be easily compact. I struggled for a solid 5 minutes to get this one in the bag.

Ultimately, it comes down to what you value. Do you need something that turns in a circle? Do you want arm rests? Do you want a pillow? Should it be compact? Do you want something that can be easily set up? If you are searching for a compact chair that can easily be carried and don’t mind set-up and break down times, then I would recommend this chair. Otherwise, you might want to look elsewhere if those aren’t your priorities.
text_fidelity_b: Compaclite High Back Oversize Steel Portable Chair for Outdoor Camping / Picnic / Hiking / Bicycling / Fishing / BBQ / Beach / Patio with Carry Bag, Royal Blue

DYJ Adjustable Right Handed Tactical Molle Modular Belt Holster for Pistol(1000D) (Black) Discounted or free item
is it good or bad?
I'll make the provider/author
either happy or sad..........
and sometimes even mad.

This is a very well-designed and strongly built holster that can hold a wide variety of pistols -- both revolvers and semi automatics. The holster is constructed of a high quality nylon and utilizes heavy-duty accessories and stitching. It is light and breathable and designed to hold many different sized and configured firearms. While I was unable to determine where it was manufactured, the quality of the construction leaves no doubt that it was designed and assembled by experts. This holster comes with a 30 day money back guarantee (or free exchange) and 24 hour customer service.

While you wouldn't typically use this to hold a sub-compact pistol, it will adequately secure a S&W Airweight, Glock 42, Walther P22, and a Kahr CM9. Stepping up, I also found it appropriate for a Springfield XD Mod 2, S&W Model 66 (or 686), and a Glock 23. It will also work with a Ruger Public Defender, a Keltec PMR-30, and the Ruger MK series. I could almost get a S&W .44 mag Backpacker in it but the sights were too high.

The reason that all of these would fit and be adequately secured is because of the triangular interior construction that is stiff enough to flex and still hold pistols of varying dimensions. Another nice feature is that the inside of the holster is composed of a smooth nylon that will not leave marks on your firearms. For the very reasonable sum of $20.00 you will receive a quality holster that is lightweight and can hold a wide variety of pistols. Tough to go wrong with this one!

I have mine mounted on the left side, which lets me easily push the lever forward with my thumb. One point, be sure and watch out for the little screw at the top of the clamp (where the bolt screws into), as it can easily fall out and go missing while doing the attachment. It's VERY small and took me awhile to find, as it bounced quite a distance. All it takes is keeping your fingers on each side during the attachment process, not a big deal as long you know to do it.

Highly recommended for those who enjoy not only the wonderful sound of a traditional bicycle bell, but also getting a good value as well.

Sabre Tactical Pepper Gel with Belt Holster for Easy Carry, Maximum Police Strength OC Spray, Quick Access Flip Top Safety, Tactical Design for Security Professionals, 18 Bursts, 18-Foot Range Every method of self-defense involves a level of awareness and confidence. Exercising "situational awareness" will often allow you to avoid placing yourself in a position where you have to protect yourself. Escape of course is the second option assuming that there is an effective way to avoid a confrontation. But if you are finally forced to bring your use of force to the situation, you must be confident of your method and how to effectively deploy it.

Many years ago I tested a Sabre product for effectiveness. Having a wife and two young daughters motivated me to find something legal that they could carry and use properly without hurting themselves in the process. The particular Sabre unit I tested DID NOT PERFORM AS ADVERTISED! I wrote a poor product review and explained why I came to that conclusion. Unfortunately my review was targeted by numerous individuals who trashed my reasoning and perspective. Yes, the Sabre products have an outstanding reputation. But not every individual unit will work as promised!

About 35 years ago I worked as a product development manager for a company lastly known as We Care America -- formerly Weapons Corporation of America (WCA). One of the products we brought to market was a pepper spray intended for self-defense use. I couldn't put my name on the recommendation until I satisfied myself as to its effectiveness. That meant that I had to be sprayed in the face. Many law enforcement organizations require their officers to be sprayed so that they understand the proper use and deployment of their spray -- and so they know what their targeted individuals will go through.

My suggestion to you is to take your unit outside the house, find an area that is not windy, hold your off-hand away from you with the palm down, and spray the back of your hand a quick burst. You should feel sharp pain on the back of your hand. If you don't, you have a defective unit. If you do, simply wash off with soap and warm water. DO NOT PUT YOUR HANDS NEAR YOUR EYES!

A unit failure can be caused by a short expiration date, poor storage, or less than optimal shipping conditions. Even on this product page Sabre states that other brands experience a 30% failure rate (University of Utah study). If your unit produces the desired irritation, shoot a full burst away from you to get an idea of how well your can is pressurized. Your spray may not go the promised 18 feet. Be aware of its particular limitations. In any event, return it immediately if it doesn't perform as advertised.

Once you determine that your individual unit is effective, make sure to view the offered free training video and then practice deploying your unit without actually spraying it. You must have confidence in both your individual unit and in yourself. Practice may seem redundant but it can be a life saver.
text_fidelity_b: Sabre Tactical Pepper Gel with Belt Holster for Easy Carry, Maximum Police Strength OC Spray, Quick Access Flip Top Safety, Tactical Design for Security Professionals, 18 Bursts, 18-Foot Range

Marmot Slate Everyday Travel Bag This is a beautifully made daily backpack. I love the styling of it so much, and the materials are obviously high quality, extremely sturdy, and is made with care. It seems like it would be fairly rain resistant given the materials. However, a few things keep this from becoming my new favorite bag.

For one, there's no zipper on the top/main compartment which keeps all of your stuff in. While the fold over part seems to keep everything in, this anxiety kept me from wanting to bring it with me on a number of recent trips where I had things inside that were both small and valuable, such as my pen from my surface tablet. I also noticed that while the fabric looks very water repellent around the top, I found it hard to get it to scrunch inside perfectly so that I would be certain no water would come in. A zipper would have really been nice.

Second, the styling of the little chest strap that clips together the two shoulder straps when you are wearing it as a backpack for a little while, is diagonal. It doesn't look intentional, but I'm pretty sure it is. It makes it look like however I position it, my backpack appears to have shifted to a weird angle. It just gives my appearance and overall sloppy, poorly put together look that make it so I would not ever really want to use the chest strap and might as well cut it off.

Other than these quibbles, the bag is thoughtfully designed and beautifully made. The small pockets are just the right size and shape for the things I would want to use them for, the padding that keeps my back comfortable and would also be protective of a tablet or laptop is very thorough, though mildly stiff, and the styling of it aside from the chest strap is absolutely beautiful, very sleek and looks like a high-end daily backpack. If you don't need your backpack to zipper, and don't mind a diagonal chest strap, this is a beautiful choice to consider.

Penn International VIS 2 Speed Reel, Gold, 30 What a great reel for big, powerful fish! If you target fish that measure in the hundreds of pounds, and you want the best tool for the job, this is your reel. In my case, it's the reel I use when we go deep for big halibut here in Alaska. This reel holds plenty of line to get to those shelves 400 feet down where the barndoors lie, with plenty of line left over to allow for long runs that those big fish make. If you hang up and break off, losing several hundred feet of line (it happens), you don't have to hang it up because the reel holds enough line to let you keep fishing.

I like the high-speed retrieve for pulling up from the deep when you need to check your bait or try something else. When you latch into a fish, though, a quick push of the button on the hub of the handle engages the more powerful lower gears, so you can really torque into the fish.

That new handle design is nice, too. It comfortably fits my hand, has a nice rubbery, no-slip texture, and helps spread the stress across the meaty part of my hand so long battles are just a little bit easier.

The open design of the "X" series frame (with no crossbars across the front of the spool) is helpful when there's a backlash to deal with (yeah, it still happens once in a while). These reels aren't cheap, but they're the best you can buy. Solid, reliable, and made in USA. No regrets here!

text_fidelity_a:
Exercise fitness sliders Dual Sided sliding discs for Gliding Discs Exercise to Enhance Coordination of Whole Body,Abdominal Exercise Equipment,Perfect for Carpet or Hardwood Floors (Black) As I started to exercise at home more, I decided that gllders/slider may be a good and affordable option to add to my exercise routine. As I have used gliders in the past at gyms, I decided these may be a good option since it was advertised to be able to use on different types of surfaces.

The sliders are a hard plastic on one side and a cushion on the flip side. You have to be careful as you need to use the cushion surface side down when using on wood floors whereas use plastic side down on most other surfaces. I tried them on artificial grass, carpeting, and wood floors. On carpeting/rugs, they work great. They slide pretty easily. They don't glide as well on other surfaces. On the turf, they barely worked and on wood floors, they worked marginally better, but not great. If you use the sliders in the wrong direction on wood floors, the plastic will likely scratch.

Note that the size of the gliders are 7 inches in diameter, which may be a tad small for men with larger hands. For using with your feet, they should work fine for most individuals.

Bottom line - they are low cost additions for home workouts, but I would only recommend if you are going to use on carpeting or a rug.
text_fidelity_b: Exercise fitness sliders Dual Sided sliding discs for Gliding Discs Exercise to Enhance Coordination of Whole Body,Abdominal Exercise Equipment,Perfect for Carpet or Hardwood Floors (Black)

text_fidelity_a:
Men Waders Waterproof Chest Waders Bootfoot Chest Wader Light Hunting Fly Fishing Waders for Men with Boots Nylon/PVC Wader Camouflage/Brown 8-14 Seems like a few fake reviews on these... how 'bout a real one?

I bought these for a week-long trip to Alaska for salmon fishing on the lower Kenai River. My expectation was that I would throw them out at the end of the trip - instead I brought them home. They mostly met my expectations but are not a 5-star product.

Cons:
- The boots fit fine, sure, but the waders were otherwise too small. I'm 6'1, 270 lbs with a 55" beer gut, and have a 33-1/2 inseam. The bottoms went up to my crotch with a little slack, but the top and suspender straps are way too short. I had the buckles on the straps adjusted to the longest length without them constantly coming out (they did occasionally) and the straps really dug in to my shoulders. The straps should be at least six inches longer, but even better the upper part of the waders should be six inches taller. It was a bit of work to get them over my belly but I got to where I could do it over a hoodie and they were snug but not tight. If your inseam is longer than 34" and you're not going to get at least size 13, these won't fit.
- I could stand in them, but crouching or sitting without keeping my legs straight was impossible. There's no stretch in the fabric.
- The top of the pocket on mine is at my navel. Plus, no Velcro or snaps to keep it closed. I got river water inside, and constantly had things falling out. I lost a rented knife I had to replace and my $300 prescription sunglasses to the river.
- The boots don't have a comfortable insole and are really hard. I bought the $15 Dr. Scholls which worked fine.
- When standing in more than a foot of water the boot uppers would collapse and cause considerable pain to the tops of my feet, often to my toes.
- No breathability. My legs and lower trunk got nice and sweaty.

Pros:
+ All the joints are sealed and taped. I didn't have a drop of water on me from the outside.
+ Boots fit well.
+ Construction and materials are good for the price in my subjective opinion.

Neutral:
~ They are unlined. I knew this before buying them. Even wearing jeans my legs got really cold. Plan appropriately.

I wish someone had written a similar review before I bought these and had them arrive. I could have made the needed modifications before I left. With that said, I would not hesitate to buy these again or recommend them to a (very warm-blooded) friend.
text_fidelity_b: Men Waders Waterproof Chest Waders Bootfoot Chest Wader Light Hunting Fly Fishing Waders for Men with Boots Nylon/PVC Wader Camouflage/Brown 8-14

text_fidelity_a: Rio Gear Portable XL Smart Cot Military Style Folding Camping Cot My dear husband is tall and wears XL clothes. He loves to camp but sleeping on the ground is not as easy for him as it once was. This cot really does set up quickly and it actually fits all of him on it! There are a few tips I want to share. First, the cot comes folded up in a handy canvas travel bag. Once you take it out of the bag, the legs at either end of the cot have to be rotated from the folded position so that they extend straight upward and then get moved 180 degrees to go under the cot. so you need a LOT of space to make this happen! I would suggest that this be done in a large open space. You probably won't be able to do it inside a tent. Once the cot is assembled, it is about a foot tall, 3 feet across, and 7 feet long. So think about those 22" legs being extended off of the 7 foot long frame as they are being rotated! If you are doing one side at a time, it will be about 9 feet long during this part of the assembly process. If you are doing both sides at once, you need a good 11 feet of space to avoid clobbering someone or knocking things around. Set the cot up outside of the tent and carry it in to be safe. The other suggestion is to loop the ends of the cot while it is not fully extended and locked into place. Once the loops are secured, you can go ahead and lock the cot at both ends to stabilize it.
text_fidelity_b: Rio Gear Portable XL Smart Cot Military Style Folding Camping Cot

text_fidelity_a:
Simmons 20-60X60 Venture Black Fmcwptripodhard/Soft Case This old bird still has some of the original low power hunting scopes made by Simmons back in the day. I always wondered why my Dad had a 4X Leupold scope on his .22 while I had a Simmons 4X. Although the Simmons did an acceptable job, it was in no way comparable to the Leupold. Of course my Dad's .22 rimfire rifle was also far superior to the Sears model that he bought for me. But believe me, I was just thrilled at age 10 to be able to go squirrel hunting. And since I trained all winter at the local armory, I could hold my own against him.

But enough of the old days. Simmons then was considered a fairly mediocre manufacturer. Now Simmons is a brand owned by Bushnell Corporation (acquired by them in 2008) which in turn is owned by Vista Outdoor. Competition in the optics market and great strides made in this technology has resulted in current offerings superior in quality and also very reasonably priced. That is an example of "value engineering" at its finest.

This Simmons spotting scope was shipped in a hard case and had the scope itself also wrapped in plastic and inside a separate soft case. Well protected indeed! A bench sized tripod is also included as are directions for both locating the instruction manual and for registering the product for potential warranty coverage. Fear not for the instruction sheet is offered in five languages.

Being an older guy and not a hunter, I don't have to worry about lugging this rather large scope through the bushes. However it does serve two needs for me. The first is that it is extremely useful when testing .22 ammo at a 100 yard range. These old eyes are not what they used to be and this Simmons scope makes it simple to track and score my shots. Most of my shooting is suppressed and testing various subsonic ammo has been interesting to say the least.

Since we live on beautiful Charlotte Harbor in Southwest Florida, Mother Nature offers us constant reminders of how the animal kingdom functions and survives. Being able to focus on long distances off our back lanai has really increased our visual reach even to the far shore. We are able to watch Bald Eagles and Osprey fish, Red Tailed Hawks and Florida Barred Owls home in on their prey, and alligators and manatees cruise through the harbor. Entertaining for us and our guests.

For roughly $150.00 this is a heck of a deal for the quality you receive. Simmons has worked its way back into being competitive with most of the mainstream firms. If you're looking for a big increase in quality, plan on spending a lot more money. In the old days we would call this "the law of diminishing returns". That means that you have to spend a lot more money just to get an incremental return in actual performance. Simmons proves that you don't have to spend that much.
text_fidelity_b: Simmons 20-60X60 Venture Black Fmcwptripodhard/Soft Case

Bilbear Adjustable Nordic Hamstring Curl Strap with Kneeling Mat,Portable Nordic Strap for Hamstring Curls,Hamstring Stretch,Crunch,Sit-ups,Nordic Curl Machine at Home,Withstand 400lbs I've been looking at Nordic Hamstring Curl straps, checking out review and pics and videos. It seems that most of the ones available on Amazon are pretty much the same, and many have the same complaints, so when I saw this one - the Bilbear Nordic Hamstring Curl Strap with Kneeling Mat - available on Vine, I ordered it.

First off, it has no chemical or rubber smells or strong smells of any kind. In addition to the strap itself, it comes with a small rubber mat for your knees, like a thinner miniature yoga mat - and a bag to put everything in.

Overall this item looked like the pics on the listing, and worked as expected. The strap is really really long, but you can use the buckle to shorten it. We found it easier to use as a foot holddown than for Nordic hamstring curls, but successfully did both repeatedly. The mat is a little thinner that my yoga mat, and it's not that large, so you need to keep your knees in the same spot on the floor if you use it. The foam is pretty comfortable, the door anchor is huge - I can't imagine a door is could slip under.

One of the complaints I read on other Nordic Hamstring Curl mats was true of this one, also - the buckle slips as you work out, so the strap gets a very tiny bit longer with each rep, but if you do a number of reps, that slippage becomes noticeable. Our other issue is how narrow the foot holders are from one side of one to the other side of the other. My husband has size 12 feet, and in his shoes, he had to keep his feet crammed together. I have much smaller but wider feet, and I found I wanted more space so my feet could be a little further apart.

Is the Bilbear Nordic Hamstring Curl Strap with Kneeling Mat for you? Well, if you prefer keeping your feet together when doing sit-ups, crunches, Nordic hamstring curls and other exercises you use a foot holddown for, you may find this very useful. Yes, the strap slips, but as far as I can tell, this is common to all similar products. I might have given this 3 stars, but because price, features and issues seem to similar to competitors, I'm giving it 4 stars based on comparable items. Happy training!
text_fidelity_b: Bilbear Adjustable Nordic Hamstring Curl Strap with Kneeling Mat,Portable Nordic Strap for Hamstring Curls,Hamstring Stretch,Crunch,Sit-ups,Nordic Curl Machine at Home,Withstand 400lbs

text_fidelity_a:
Kelty Grand Mesa Backpacking Tent (2020 Update) Picked up this tent after LOTS of searching and watching reviews. This tent is heavier than what I wanted for backpacking, however, I think the trade offs will be positive.
First off, the construction is very good out of the bag. All seams and tie out points are sealed with seam tape. No loose threads. The fly and tub are manufactured with a nice weight nylon, not too thin, and not too thick.
The newly designed corner sleeves for the poles are nice, this helps to pull the tent body nice and taut. Great design.
I like the color scheme as well, not too bright, but not drab either.
The aluminum pole segments seem to be shorter than most other tents, this should make it easy to pack in my back pack. I still have not decided if I will roll everything up in the storage bag and pack it vertically. Or use a stuff sack and shove the tent in the bottom of my pack and store the poles on the outside of the pack.
The vestibule is nice. It is not huge, but, it has plenty of room for shoes and some other items that you do not want to store in the tent. The ONE thing that sold me on this tent, is the way the vestibule zips open and closed. The last dome style I had with a vestibule, it zipped right down the middle. This made it hard to get to, as you had to basically crawl most of the way out of the tent to unzip it. This vestibule unzips right at the side of the entrance, which makes it super easy to open and close! AWESOME design!! More tent manufacturers need to use this design.
The only two cons I have right out of the packaging, is:
1. The tent IS on the heavy side, at almost 5 pounds. But, if you were backpacking with a friend or spouse, you could split up the pieces and make it lighter. But for a solo hiker, it is heavy. However, with the room you get, it is a good trade off.
2. The fly tie downs were just short loops of cordage that did not even reach the ground, and you cannot use the stakes to stake them out. Both sides and the rear are like this. I fixed this issue by just adding a length of cordage to all 3 spots.
I removed the supplied plastic line adjusters and just tied a taut line hitch on all pieces of cordage.
I will update after a few uses if need be.
text_fidelity_b: Kelty Grand Mesa Backpacking Tent (2020 Update)

text_fidelity_a: Portable Camping Lights, FOGEEK Mini Rechargeable Tent Light, Night Light, Emergency Light, 5200mAh Power Bank, Water Resistant, Fireproof, Magnet Base, 5 Light Modes, Best for Reading, Hiking Small and lightweight, be sure you have your 3 AAA batteries for each of the pair on standby or you won't be able to use the bright lights.  They are packed in a single box and my first impression was that these were cheap dollar store products.  After installing the batteries, I found them to actually be fine working lights which can be hung from inside a tent if you like.  Because they are quite flat in design, they will not take up much air space so you may not hit your head if you awaken in the dark and sit upright.  The literature states that the light will operate for 3.5 hours at full intensity, 4 hours at mid level and 12 hours at low light level.  I don't know about using the flash or SOS modes but at any rate, I would take an ample supply of batteries with me to assure that I have light if needed during camping expeditions.  Happy to have these for summer storms when we have a tendency to experience power outages in my area.  The LED light is bright but not blinding due to the frosted white plastic.  I've recently seen these sold under an assortment of names and would definitely be sure to only get them with the SOS function like these. Sample was provided for evaluation.
text_fidelity_b: Portable Camping Lights, FOGEEK Mini Rechargeable Tent Light, Night Light, Emergency Light, 5200mAh Power Bank, Water Resistant, Fireproof, Magnet Base, 5 Light Modes, Best for Reading, Hiking

text_fidelity_a:
SHIMANO PD-M324 SPD Dual Platform Pedal These are the only pedals of this variety I've tried. I have two pairs. I use these on my "no attachment" vintage road bikes - bikes that I lock up with a cheap cable lock, and if I come out and the bike is gone, I won't even break stride or spend one minute worrying about it. I do ride a lot and I put a lot of miles on a contemporary road bike with Garmin Vector pedals, which are universe away in form and even purpose. That should be enough background to know where I'm coming from.

First, here's what I love about these pedals. I used to ride my ghetto version of a hybrid bike to nearby stores. That bike is just an old, all-rigid Hard Rock MTB on which I put fenders, a road saddle, and Specialized Nimbus tires. It's so slow that even riding a mile and a half to the grocery store kinda bummed me out. But that was the only bike I could jump onto in street shoes. That's how I arrived at this pedal. I put these on my two old road bikes and now that quick jaunt to the store is much more to my taste.

These pedals are easy to clip in/out, set up, operate. I will say that the pedals I took off my disposable old road bikes, PD-M520L, were slightly easier to clip into and had better clearance. So the switch is a compromise. Basically this M324 is a pedal that does two things, but neither quite as well as the pedals that do just one of the things. That's fine with me.

PROS:
cheap
easy
cleats or any other shoe

CON:
heavy
less ground clearance (I touched down once and have since been careful with these pedals)
closer to road pedals than SPD or platform for ease of getting started - i personally have gotten to where i can clip in w/o looking but it's not as confident with pure SPD pedals, where i just mindlessly mash my foot onto the pedal and it works every time

Overall I'd say that if you want a pedal that is a compromise between platform and SPD, this will make just about anyone happy. It's hard to imagine someone with that as their first criterion who also wants high performance. This is the first pedal of this type I've tried and I didn't even bother trying a different model for my second pair - they are plenty good enough. If they are not the cheapest available they must at least be in the running. Really can't go wrong.
text_fidelity_b: SHIMANO PD-M324 SPD Dual Platform Pedal

The protective coating scratches and stains but; it can be removed and cleaned if you have the time. I like to keep my things looking brand new. I may remove the coating at some point.

The sheath is not the greatest but at least you don’t have to buy one.

The good: it comes with a sheath, a sharpening stone, and a fire steel. You don’t get that with $500 knives.

It can accomplish every task a $500 knife can.

You can sell the knife/knives for what you paid; if you want to upgrade.

You can keep them to loan out or for a buddy to use.

Best of all is the price. You get to test out your skills for less than $30 bucks with this knife.

Canway Bike Tail Light 168 Lumens Super Bright Red/Blue Bicycle Light 500mah Lithium Battery Rear Bike Light USB C Rechargeable 5 Modes Waterproof Safety for Road, Mountain, Night Riding Great light! It's really bright and the various mode are very useful. I live in CA so I can only use the red color. I can tell it really gets peoples attention because people making right turns over the bike lane actually waits behind me on a red light. :-)

Battery lasts for about 4-5 hours (my ride is 1.30 hours/day). Charging is simple. I use a regular charger base (not the fast charging) because I am not sure if this unit can deal with high charge rate. I had bad luck with other things like usb headphones that just couldn't handle fast charging. The regular charging speed is about a few hours. So I usually charge it after a few rides for 2-3 hours.

Mounting is easy. I ride on city streets, so I cannot tell if the thing with stay on after a very bumpy ride. The latch seems pretty solid.

The unit itself doesn't feel very sturdy (light plasticky feel), so I am not sure how it will fare if I dropped it on a paved road. So I am careful when I take it out or put it back in the mount.
text_fidelity_b: Canway Bike Tail Light 168 Lumens Super Bright Red/Blue Bicycle Light 500mah Lithium Battery Rear Bike Light USB C Rechargeable 5 Modes Waterproof Safety for Road, Mountain, Night Riding

text_fidelity_a:
Black Diamond Revolt Headlamp Everyone I know uses Black Diamond headlamps, but I've always owned Petzl. I've always wondered if I'd like BD better. When I had a bag stolen that had my newest Petzl headlamp in it I thought I'd try out the Black Diamond Revolt. For a headlamp that can recharge batteries with a USB cable it was a really good price, so I pulled the trigger on it. It has adequate lumens for my purposes (backpacking, evening hiking, and use around the house), although it isn't quite as bright as my similarly priced Petzl models. It has an awesome, fully adjustable dimmer setting that is the one thing that stands out as better than any other headlamp I've used. It also has a red LED setting, which is important to me - I actually find that I use the red LED way more than the white for late night use. As far as features go, I'm happy with everything you get with the Revolt.

The more I've used this headlamp though, I have a few minor complaints compared to similar offerings from Petzl. As mentioned above, I use the red LED setting often. It's great when you want to maintain night vision. I also like that if I wake up in the middle of the night and quickly use my lamp, the red LED wakes me up less than a bright white light. The problem for me is that the red setting on the Revolt is way too dim. It's hard to see anything that's more than just a few feet away. This makes it so that I can't use it in as many situations as I could with my old Petzl. I definitely wish it were brighter in the red mode.

Another feature on most headlamps is an adjustable angle setting where you can click it up and down to choose how high the lamp points. The Revolt has solid detents that seem like they will hold up well over time. This is kind of splitting hairs, but I don't like how widely spaced the detents are. It always seems to be too high or too low. YMMV, but I liked Petzl again here for the finer adjustments. I have to fiddle with the Revolt more often.

On the other hand, I'm not gentle with my headlamps. I use them constantly at home and work and any time I backpack or travel. I cram them into bags, toss them around a bit, bump them on things and occasionally drop them. It's hard to say, but friends that I work with and backpack with seem to have better luck with their Black Diamond lamps' durability. The Revolt is solidly built and seems to use batteries very efficiently. It seems like it might be a little sturdier and maybe last longer than my previous Petzl lamps, but that's purely a guess at this point. We'll see, but so far so good. I'm basing that more on friends' experiences with BD lamps. Either way, it's certainly no worse.

Overall, I think this is a pretty good headlamp. It's a solid value for the price and does everything I want it to. I'll continue to use it pretty happily, but when it comes time to replace it, I'll go back to Petzl. Even if the Revolt is a little sturdier, I like the way Petzl lamps work and feel. They're less clunky and they just seems to have their headlamps really dialed across the board. They're comfortable, intuitive and very well designed. Get a Revolt if you want a solid, functional headlamp, but get a Petzl if you really want to love it.
text_fidelity_b: Black Diamond Revolt Headlamp
